target_customer: Companies with large volumes of video such as robotics, security and industrial monitoring teams that find frontier video models too expensive
problem: Frontier video language models can read video but are too costly or slow to run at industrial volume, so most video stays unreadable to machines.
business_model: Custom distilled small video models per customer task plus an open weights model, Marlin; commercial terms not published

founders.name: Shubham Sharma
founders.background_notes: YC page: NeurIPS spotlight paper on offline RL; sole listed founder, team of 2.

technical_complexity.rationale: Distilling a frontier video model into a 2B parameter open model that is reported to match Gemini 2.5 Flash on dense captioning and temporal grounding is research heavy for a two person team; the base model reportedly comes from Qwen.

defensibility.rationale: The base model and distillation approach are open and large labs can ship cheaper small video models; customer specific post-training data could become a moat later.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Frontier labs and Twelve Labs already sold video understanding in 2026; no outcome yet.

market_need_then: Video volume is large and frontier video models are costly at scale, per the company; no independent demand data found.

identity.logo: not described by any source found

branding.community_and_virality: Marlin 2B model appears on Hugging Face and fal.ai, where sources attribute it to NemoStation; the relation to Kailash Labs is unconfirmed.

brand_strength.rationale: No brand coverage found and the Marlin model is published under a different name, NemoStation, which splits identity.

outcome_analysis: Kailash Labs is a two person Fall 2026 company in Bengaluru building small video reasoning models; it is active with no exit, and it is too early to judge. The YC page and the company website describe different offerings (video models versus robot workcells), which is an unresolved inconsistency.
notes: Company website content (robot cells for hard to staff stations, pilots of seven days) does not match the YC page (video reasoning models); possibly an old or different site. Funding unverified: Dealroom lists a 125k seed and Caplight lists 500k total with an accelerator round dated 2026-10-01; not recorded as rounds. Competitor search found only Twelve Labs era vendor pages and comparison blogs with no dating near the Fall 2026 batch, so the list is empty. Founder claims are from the YC page only.
